item.title: Finite Difference Methods: Marching Forward or Solving Together
item.description:
Why This Matters

A derivative price can be computed two equivalent ways: as a risk-neutral expectation, or as the solution of a PDE. This is the Feynman-Kac result, which I explored in the earlier article. Monte Carlo is the natural way to handle the expectation, and the previous article worked through techniques for making it more efficient. Here I want to look at the other side, where the price is the solution of a PDE and we solve it on a grid.
